questions.stem: In CLZ-130, Azure CLI supplies a user token. What pins the AzureRM target subscription?

options.A: The environment tag.

optionExplanations.A: Tags describe resources rather than select subscriptions.
optionExplanations.B: The provider receives an explicit deployment target.
optionExplanations.C: Lesson identity affects naming, not authentication.
optionExplanations.D: File naming does not select cloud context.

questions.stem: Azure CLI can sign in, but resource-group creation returns 403. Which issue is most relevant?

options.A: HCL indentation alone.
options.C: Authorization at the target Azure scope.

optionExplanations.A: Formatting is not RBAC.
optionExplanations.B: Navigation does not grant permissions.
optionExplanations.C: A valid identity can still lack the required action.
optionExplanations.D: Low cost does not grant create authority.

questions.stem: Which command displays the provider requirements used by this configuration?

options.A: terraform output -raw location

optionExplanations.A: That reads a result, not the dependency tree.
optionExplanations.B: That reads Azure regions.
optionExplanations.C: That proposes resource removal.
optionExplanations.D: It identifies provider dependencies.

questions.stem: The created group has an Azure ID beginning /subscriptions/<guid>/. What should <guid> match?

options.A: The intended subscription_id passed to Terraform.

optionExplanations.A: The resource ID exposes the actual subscription boundary.
optionExplanations.B: Region names are not subscription GUIDs.
optionExplanations.C: That contains an environment label.
optionExplanations.D: Provider versions do not identify subscriptions.

questions.stem: Several subscriptions share the same visible name. Which selector should the learner use?

options.A: The first alphabetical display name.

optionExplanations.A: That can identify the wrong subscription.
optionExplanations.B: It avoids display-name ambiguity.
optionExplanations.C: Region proximity does not select a subscription.
optionExplanations.D: A resource tag is not a subscription identity.

questions.stem: Terraform reports an authentication problem after an earlier CLI login. What read helps diagnose the session?

options.A: az group delete

optionExplanations.A: Deleting objects is not authentication diagnosis.
optionExplanations.B: Formatting does not refresh authentication.
optionExplanations.C: It tests whether CLI can obtain a token for the active context.
optionExplanations.D: Tag values do not repair tokens.

questions.stem: Which authentication choice matches the interactive CLZ-130 pattern?

options.A: Put the access token in locals.tf.
options.B: Store a client secret in README.md.
options.C: Use the group name as a password.
options.D: Use the authenticated Azure CLI session.

optionExplanations.A: Tokens should not be committed.
optionExplanations.B: Documentation is not a secret store.
optionExplanations.C: Resource names are not credentials.
optionExplanations.D: The provider can use CLI identity without embedding credentials.

questions.stem: The input's GUID regex accepts a value. What remains unproven?

options.A: Whether the identity has access to that subscription.
options.D: Whether null is supported by the declaration.

optionExplanations.A: String validation does not query Azure authorization.
optionExplanations.B: The regex checks that shape.
optionExplanations.C: The regex explicitly permits them.
optionExplanations.D: The nullable input allows null.

questions.stem: Which file's provider block directs Azure control-plane operations for the lab?

options.A: README.md

optionExplanations.A: Markdown documents rather than configures the provider.
optionExplanations.B: It configures azurerm and its subscription input.
optionExplanations.C: An example file is not automatically the live provider block.
optionExplanations.D: The variable supplies an input, while the provider block consumes it to target requests.

questions.stem: Interactive user login is unsuitable for unattended CI. Which production pattern fits the lesson?

options.A: A shared personal token in Git.
options.D: Use the subscription GUID as the only authentication credential.

optionExplanations.A: That exposes credentials and weakens accountability.
optionExplanations.B: Azure requires an authorized identity.
optionExplanations.C: Federation provides workload authentication without a stored long-lived secret.
optionExplanations.D: A target identifier is not proof of identity.

questions.stem: Why does CLZ-130 create an empty resource group?

options.A: To prove all VM sizes are available.

optionExplanations.A: A group does not test compute capacity.
optionExplanations.B: No storage account is declared.
optionExplanations.C: No password resource exists.
optionExplanations.D: It provides a small managed object for the authentication path.

questions.stem: What does terraform init prepare before provider-backed planning?

options.A: The working directory and required provider dependencies.

optionExplanations.A: Initialization makes the selected plugins available.
optionExplanations.B: Provider installation grants no RBAC role.
optionExplanations.C: Init does not apply the resource plan.
optionExplanations.D: There is no VM in this module.

questions.stem: Why destroy CLZ-120 before following CLZ-130's prerequisite guidance?

options.A: Both lessons require the exact same state file.
options.B: To keep the learning lifecycle and remaining resources understandable.
options.C: Azure allows only one resource group per subscription.
options.D: CLI authentication stops working when two groups exist.

optionExplanations.A: They are separate root modules.
optionExplanations.B: The lessons use independent managed boundaries.
optionExplanations.C: Subscriptions can contain multiple groups.
optionExplanations.D: Group count does not govern authentication.

questions.stem: A production identity only needs to manage one approved resource-group scope. Which choice fits least privilege?

options.A: Grant tenant-wide rights by default.
options.C: Grant the required role at that scope.

optionExplanations.A: That exceeds the stated need.
optionExplanations.B: That broadens privilege and reduces accountability.
optionExplanations.C: Narrow scope limits authority beyond the workload.
optionExplanations.D: Regions do not grant RBAC permissions.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish provider source and local name
questions.stem: What does hashicorp/azurerm identify in required_providers?

options.A: An Azure tenant.
options.D: The source address of the AzureRM provider.

optionExplanations.A: It is a Terraform provider address.
optionExplanations.B: Resource names are configured separately.
optionExplanations.C: It does not identify Azure billing.
optionExplanations.D: The source tells Terraform which provider implementation to install.

questions.stem: A valid token belongs to a different tenant than the intended subscription. What should be checked?

options.A: CLI tenant context and access to the target subscription.

optionExplanations.A: Authentication must align with the deployment boundary.
optionExplanations.B: Naming cannot repair tenant context.
optionExplanations.C: Metadata cannot change identity.
optionExplanations.D: Names can be ambiguous and do not replace tenant and access checks.

questions.stem: Why pass the same intended subscription ID during cleanup?

options.A: Destroy needs a new subscription every time.
options.B: Destroy must address the same managed Azure boundary.
options.C: It tells Terraform to erase CLI credentials.

optionExplanations.A: That is not the intended lifecycle.
optionExplanations.B: Cleanup should not drift to another target.
optionExplanations.C: Subscription targeting is not credential revocation.
optionExplanations.D: Deletion remains subject to authorization.

questions.stem: Which pair most directly supports that Terraform and CLI target the intended subscription?

options.A: Provider source address and version constraint.
options.C: Checked CLI account ID and the deployed group's subscription ID.

optionExplanations.A: Dependency information does not prove the live subscription boundary.
optionExplanations.B: Neither proves a subscription match.
optionExplanations.C: Both expose the real context boundary.
optionExplanations.D: Local names do not prove cloud targeting.

questions.stem: Why keep the committed .terraform.lock.hcl when repeating authentication tests?

options.A: It encrypts the user's CLI token.
options.B: It grants delete access to the group.
options.C: It chooses the active Azure tenant.
options.D: It preserves reviewed provider selections and checksums.

optionExplanations.A: It is not a credential vault.
optionExplanations.B: Dependency metadata grants no RBAC role.
optionExplanations.C: Account context is configured separately.
optionExplanations.D: The lock file records dependency choices.

questions.stem: Does terraform providers schema -json by itself prove which subscription a resource was created in?

options.A: No; it describes provider schemas rather than live resource targeting.
options.B: Yes, schemas enumerate all deployed subscription IDs.
options.C: Yes, it replaces az account show.
options.D: Only if the output is discarded.

optionExplanations.A: Use actual context and resource IDs for that evidence.
optionExplanations.B: Schema describes supported structure, not deployment inventory.
optionExplanations.C: It cannot show the CLI's selected account.
optionExplanations.D: Discarding schema output supplies no new evidence.

questions.stem: The lab input permits null and mentions ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID. What is the safe practice for its live exercise?

options.A: Assume null always means the correct subscription.
options.B: Supply and verify an explicit intended subscription ID.
options.C: Use the tenant ID in its place.

optionExplanations.A: Implicit context must not substitute for target review.
optionExplanations.B: The README asks for a pinned target for plan/apply/destroy.
optionExplanations.C: A tenant ID is not a subscription selector.
optionExplanations.D: That prevents the intended provider-backed exercise.

questions.stem: Which production design does CLZ-130 recommend for privileged automation?

options.A: Give every pipeline Owner permanently.
options.B: Use one broad identity with no distinction between preview and execution.
options.C: Separate plan and apply identities where appropriate.
options.D: Store all tokens in public plan logs.

optionExplanations.A: That ignores least privilege.
optionExplanations.B: The production guidance calls for deliberate privilege separation.
optionExplanations.C: Their required permissions can differ.
optionExplanations.D: That exposes credentials.

questions.stem: A user has Reader on the target subscription. What does that role normally allow here?

options.A: Creating and deleting any group.
options.D: Reading metadata, not creating the resource group.

optionExplanations.A: Those need write/delete permissions.
optionExplanations.B: Reader does not grant role-assignment writes.
optionExplanations.C: That is beyond Reader's actions.
optionExplanations.D: Reader excludes resource write operations.

questions.stem: Provider authentication fails repeatedly. What should precede changing Terraform source?

options.A: Inspect the error, active account, tenant, and role scope.
options.D: Switch to any working production subscription.

optionExplanations.A: Diagnose context before altering reviewed configuration.
optionExplanations.B: That conceals rather than resolves the cause.
optionExplanations.C: Credential sharing is not the intended fix.
optionExplanations.D: A convenient subscription may be unauthorized for the lab.

questions.stem: What does az group exists returning false after the documented destroy support?

options.A: Every object in every subscription is gone.
options.B: The named group is absent in the checked subscription.
options.C: The CLI user's account was deleted.

optionExplanations.A: The query is scoped to a group and context.
optionExplanations.B: This is independent Azure cleanup evidence.
optionExplanations.C: Group existence does not test account deletion.
optionExplanations.D: Azure reads do not report local plugin installation.

sources.title: Manage resource groups with Azure CLI

questions.stem: Why is no authentication credential placed in the lesson's Terraform code?

options.A: Terraform supports only anonymous Azure calls.
options.B: The resource group never requires access control.
options.C: The CLI session supplies identity outside source.
options.D: No credential is needed because the group is empty.

optionExplanations.A: Azure operations need authentication.
optionExplanations.B: Resource groups remain RBAC-protected.
optionExplanations.C: The example avoids embedding a credential in versioned files.
optionExplanations.D: An empty group is still an authenticated Azure control-plane resource.

questions.stem: Does features {} in this provider automatically grant extra Azure permissions?

options.A: Yes, it grants Contributor at subscription scope.
options.D: No; provider settings do not create role assignments.

optionExplanations.A: A provider block is not an RBAC grant.
optionExplanations.B: It does not replace identity context.
optionExplanations.C: An environment label cannot grant authority.
optionExplanations.D: Authorization is controlled by Azure RBAC.

questions.stem: An authorized owner just granted the needed role, but plan still fails. Which response is reasonable?

options.A: Recheck scope and allow the grant time to propagate.
options.D: Delete the dependency lock file to get permissions.

optionExplanations.A: Fresh grants can take time before requests succeed.
optionExplanations.B: No RDP resource is involved.
optionExplanations.C: A metadata label is not a role.
optionExplanations.D: Provider selection does not create RBAC rights.

questions.stem: Changing location to westeurope should change which authentication fact?

options.A: The signed-in user automatically.
options.B: None by itself; it changes deployment location.

optionExplanations.A: Identity comes from authentication context.
optionExplanations.B: Region input does not change identity or subscription selection.
optionExplanations.C: Location does not choose a directory.
optionExplanations.D: Roles are separate assignments.

questions.stem: The CLI can read the subscription but Terraform cannot delete its group. What is the key distinction?

options.A: Successful reads imply all writes.
options.C: Read access and delete permission are separate actions.
options.D: Deleting local tfplan grants delete permission.

optionExplanations.A: RBAC does not work that way.
optionExplanations.B: It can when authorized.
optionExplanations.C: A role must authorize the needed operation at scope.
optionExplanations.D: A local file cannot alter Azure authorization.
